title: Incident Suite sample log labels
description: Ground truth for eval/run_eval.py: what the agents should find in each sample log. Line numbers are 1-based. For text and JSON-lines files they are file line numbers; for CSV, TSV, Parquet and JSON documents they are data row numbers (the CSV/TSV header row is not counted, the first record is row 1).

format.description: The inner format. For .gz files, the format after decompressing

generated.description: True for files made by sample_logs/make_samples.py (Parquet, gzip, the 50k log)

expected_top_severity.description: The worst severity across expected_issues, or none for a healthy log

expect_ticket.description: True if and only if at least one issue is critical

expect_slack.description: True if and only if at least one issue is medium or worse

context_lines.description: Non-error lines that explain the cause, e.g. a deploy or config change just before the errors

noise_lines.description: Harmless WARN/ERROR lines the agents should NOT report as issues (tests false positives)

same_signature_as.description: For repeat logs: the file whose critical issue has the same signature (tests JIRA dedupe)

evidence_lines.description: Every line or row that shows this issue. For big generated logs, a representative sample of up to 10

signature_hint.description: A short phrase from the main error lines, e.g. 'Connection refused'. Helps the eval match a found issue to this one

expected_fix_keywords.description: Words a good fix should mention, e.g. ['pool', 'max_size']. Used for a rough fix-quality score
